Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:49: Therefore a person must rectify his soul so that it be a throne for YHVH, the Cause of causes, to rest upon; and therefore he must do this out of love so that He cling to him. So it is written in Sefer Chasidim (siman 73), that one of the things that hinders prayer from being heard is if he is not pure — and according to the view of Tosafot (Chullin 122b, s.v. "le-gabel"), who hold that for prayer immersion is required but for Torah it is not required, there is good reason for this on the level of the secret, and it is proper as a practical matter — for the Torah, because of its great rank, being in the male world, has the power to withstand the kelipah, and does not receive impurity, like fire. However, prayer is the seeking of mercy and supplication, and requires the heart's intention, and while one is impure, his intention will surely be confused; therefore one must be careful regarding it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:50: Regarding the secret of the mikveh, it is already known what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (parashat Pinchas) and in the Tikkunim (39a), that it is in the secret of the Supernal, nine points on each side, etc.; see there. And the secret of the mikveh is the secret of YHVH — for the mikveh contains forty se'ah, and likewise YHVH has four letters, each letter comprising ten — this is the secret of "the mikveh [hope] of Israel is YHVH." And understand by this what they said (Yoma 8:9), just as a mikveh purifies the impure, so the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies Israel — namely, the purification of their souls, which cling to His Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:51: It follows that one who immerses is truly bound to YHVH, to purify his body and his soul — his body in the water, and his soul in the spirituality of the Name resting there. And through this, even if the water is cold, it will not harm him — for since he is bound to YHVH, it is impossible that harm come to him, as the Psalmist said (Psalms 91:2), "I say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress," etc., "for He shall deliver you from the snare of the fowler" — namely, from cold and other mishaps — and the rest of that psalm: "for He shall command His angels concerning you," etc., "they shall bear you upon their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone," and the rest of the psalm.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:52: However, one must perform the commandment with joy, for if he does not serve with joy he is punished, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:53: It is also fitting to contemplate repentance, for repentance is in the secret of the mikveh, and the soul too flows from there; and when a person sins, repentance departs, and likewise the soul departs from over the person, and he is far from clinging. Through a person's entering the mikveh, which is a square "mem" — the Mother [Imma] who rests upon the building — the Mother, who is repentance [teshuvah, "the heh returns"], and the vav returns and crouches upon the sons — so too the soul returns to the person, and the Cause of causes rests upon his soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:54: I heard from a certain elder sage that one who is impure does not have the soul resting within him until he enters the mikveh, and this is correct for the reason I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:55: The reason the soul departs is that, because of its great fineness, any trace of blemish found in the body prevents it from being able to rest within it, until it returns to the source of the soul and is included there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:56: This is a matter a person must intend in his immersion — that he enters, through the secret of his soul, into those supernal waters that are in the secret of the World to Come, and he is hidden in the supernal concealment, which is in Binah, and Imma conceals him within her wings. And just as it is explained in the Tikkunim (39a) that the Shechinah immerses and is purified in the mikveh waters, so Ze'ir Anpin surely immerses — and one should intend that he ascends there in the secret of the vav, and his spirit and soul are purified from every blemish. He should also intend that the spark of the Shechinah clothed within him is likewise purified from the blemish it received, and through the immersion he strips off from himself the spirit of impurity and is clothed with the secret of the soul that had departed — and immersion is a great aid in acquiring the soul, for purity is from within and holiness from without; see what I explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:57: You already know that the law requires water in which one's whole body can rise [be immersed] (Pesachim 109a) — meaning that it covers his entire body without any part remaining outside the water, even the width of a hair's breadth — for since the outside retains some hold over some limb, however slight, from there his impurity spreads to all his limbs, and it is as though he had not immersed at all. And when he immerses and enters, all his 248 limbs, within the forty se'ah, he strips off from himself every trace of the spirit of impurity — for by the power of Imma, the great eagle with the wings that fears not the vulture of prey and the like, the outside forces are nullified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:58: There is a further reason: immersion in the mikveh is like returning vessels to the kiln so that they be purified and refined, and upon coming out of the kiln they are new; so too, a person entering the mikveh is in order to be included and to have his blemished soul and blemished limbs return to the place from which they emerged, and there they are hidden away like an embryo hidden in its mother's womb, over which the eye of the outside forces has no power, and it is guarded from every mishap and chance occurrence, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Niddah 30b) on "as in the days of God He watched over me" (Job 29:2), regarding the fetus in its mother's womb. And when a person emerges from the mikveh, his limbs and his soul have been rectified, and he is new, and the outside forces have no share in him, and the person will feel within himself a new spirit from the spark of the soul that has returned to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:59: It is fitting that before entering the mikveh, he contemplate repentance for his sins, and if possible confess as well, so that no share remains for the outside forces in the soul. This matter is clear — for just as, to purify oneself from ordinary impurity, a nocturnal emission, a flux, and the like, nothing must intervene between him and the water, for the reason I explained, so too regarding the purification of sin, which is a more spiritual impurity clinging to the soul until it causes blemish and darkness within it — a washing is needed to remove it with lye and soap through repentance, and nothing should intervene from within, in his soul. For I have already explained that the essential purpose of immersion for a penitent is to purify himself from his sins and restore his soul to him; if so, for this he must set his heart to repent of his sins entirely, and not immerse while some of the sins still remain in his hand — for the immersion will not avail him for the purification of his sins, as explained, until he abandons them completely and entirely. This is in the manner that will be explained, with God's help, in the matter of repentance, that the matter of prayer and supplication for forgiveness of sin requires that he first rectify, as much as is within his power, his sins, and only afterward pray for them; therefore it is fitting that he confess before entering the mikveh, or at least contemplate it. And in Sefer Chasidim they wrote that it is fitting to immerse three times, corresponding to chatat (sin), avon (iniquity), and pesha (transgression).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:60: When the mikveh water is cold and he suffers from it, he should intend what our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 5a), that the World to Come is attained only through suffering, this being one of the three good gifts that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave to Israel; and immersion is an allusion to the World to Come, and therefore requires suffering. And by accepting upon himself the aspect of coldness, which is the judgment flowing from Gevurah, he merits the light of life, the good hidden away above in the World to Come — this being (Proverbs 6:23), "and the way of life is the reproofs of discipline" — and this is mercy [rachamim]; and so you find (Zohar, parashat Pekudei 247a) that souls do not enter the upper Garden of Eden until they immerse in the River of Fire.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:61: One who is careful to perform the immersion at its proper time will surely not be harmed by any injurious force, for "one who guards a commandment shall know no evil thing." But if he is compelled by circumstance to let its time pass, or is negligent in the commandment without any compulsion, it is possible that the commandment will not protect him from being saved from the mishaps of the time. And if he was negligent in performing it at its time, let him hasten to repent, and not let the impurity grow old within his soul, for afterward it will be difficult to separate it — in the manner of what is written (Zohar, parashat Pinchas 227b), "before the hoary head you shall rise" (Leviticus 19:32) — before the evil inclination grows old within him — and let him trust in the Lord, for one who comes to purify himself is aided, and no harm at all shall befall him, for the reason explained: that in purifying himself, he purifies also his soul and his spirit, which are the supernal portion, and since he purifies the parts of the holy sparks, he surely is aided.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:62: One must think, in performing this commandment, with fear and love, in the manner required generally of the commandments, as the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 25b) — fear, that he not be negligent in performing it, and that he fear the Supernal King who commands it, and it is fitting that he not transgress His will; and he should think that if a king of flesh and blood were to command this, how careful he would be to perform it, so as not to transgress the king's command. And out of love, that he desire the King's love, that out of love for Him, even if He commanded him to throw himself into a fiery furnace like Abraham, he would cast himself in — how much more so, since all the King's commandments are for our own benefit, to grant us an inheritance in a world that is entirely long, as it says (Deuteronomy 6:25), "and it shall be righteousness for us if we take care to perform," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:63: Even in this world he has a good reward for his labor, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 22b), that its special property is length of days, in these words: Rabbi Yannai said, I have heard that some are strict about it, and I have heard that some are lenient about it, and whoever is strict with himself about it has his days and years lengthened. — end of quotation. The reason is that its secret is in the place of length of life, namely "al Hashem" ["over the Lord"], as explained in the Zohar (parashat Acharei 79b), and the first three [sefirot] are considered as one. Also, one who performs the commandment with the same desire as his desire for life — for he is thereby in the commandment which is YHVH, the source of life, and he is bound to the Cause of causes bound to YHVH — surely lengthens his days through this intention.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:64: He must be joyful in performing the commandment, as one going to earn much money is joyful over it — so he should be joyful in the commandments, for he is bound to His great Name YHVH and to the supernal life, and rectifies his soul; as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:162), "I rejoice at Your word, like one who finds great spoil," and says (Habakkuk 3:18), "and I shall exult in YHVH."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:65: Regarding the plain meaning of Rabbi Yannai's statement, Rashi explained that "they are lenient about it" — in bathhouses or in pouring nine kav [of water]; "they are strict about it" — in forty se'ah. Tosafot wrote that although they said in the Gemara, immersion [after nocturnal emission] was nullified [as a requirement for Torah study] according to Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira — this refers specifically to Torah, but for prayer it is required.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:66: The students of Rabbeinu Yonah wrote on this matter, that what is said there in the Gemara, brought by the Rif, peace be upon him — words of Torah do not receive impurity, as it is said, "is not My word like fire," etc. — our sages, of blessed memory, said, some explain that there is no difference between the Shema and other readings, and for everything we say, words of Torah do not receive impurity — but this is not correct, for surely they said this only regarding the Shema alone, but for other words of Torah it is forbidden, for it is said (Numbers 15:31), "for he has despised the word of the Lord," etc. — this refers to one who recites words of Torah in filthy alleyways — and they were stricter about this than about other cases of "karet" [excision], for in all other cases of karet, being cut off atones, but in this case it does not atone, but rather even though he is cut off, his sin remains with him. — end of quotation. It follows from their words that Torah is more stringent than prayer, and that reciting Torah while impure — one's body being impure — is more severe than reciting Torah in filthy alleyways, for which there is a punishment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:67: They further wrote there that the Rif wrote, and Rabbeinu Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, wrote: since there is no explicit Gemara on this matter, follow the custom of all Israel, that all who have had a seminal emission, even if they have no water, do not pray until they wash. And they wrote there that this washing is not in forty se'ah but in nine kav, and the nine kav must be poured over him from a vessel that can pour them over him without any interruption — and this is also proven in the Mishnayot of Taharot (Mikvaot 3:3-4). What the Gaon, of blessed memory, wrote — that one does not pray until washing — does not appear correct to my teacher, the rabbi, may his Rock and Redeemer protect him; if he has no water, or even if he has water but does not immerse or wash, even so he does not lose his prayer because of this, for surely, even though prayer is more acceptable with immersion, according to all opinions he should not lose his prayer because of it. And so Rabbeinu Moshe [Maimonides], of blessed memory, wrote, that all the heads of the academies of Babylonia were astonished at him, why he was so lenient regarding the immersions of one who had a seminal emission, and he, of blessed memory, answered them that he had never nullified it, but rather that he could only write in his composition what follows strictly from the halachah; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:68: Rabbeinu Yonah's words on this are according to his own view, that he wrote that words of Torah are more stringent than prayer, and therefore prayer should not be nullified so that its time not pass, but according to his view words of Torah should not be recited [while impure].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:69: I say that one who fears Heaven should fulfill all opinions — when his body is healthy he should be strict and use forty se'ah, and if his body is weak or in the cold season, he should pour upon himself nine kav of warm water; in any case, if he is compelled by circumstance and immersion is not available to him, he should not nullify Torah or prayer because of this, for the lenient opinions are worthy to be relied upon in time of pressing need. And at night, before he has immersed, he should not refrain from rising at the night watch to engage in Torah because he is impure, for the other decisors are worthy to be relied upon. A person should not be idle from words of Torah, and should consider those hours like a day when he is ill, when he certainly would not nullify Torah and prayer; and whoever is strict with himself not to engage in Torah and prayer without immersion, even when ill, holds a mistaken view and it is not fitting to rely upon it — and as I have written, this was the practice of our master Rabbi Isaac Luria Ashkenazi, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:70: Further, we find in the Torah that all of a person's purification, whether from his impurity or from his soiling, and the washing of his garments, is all through water, as it is written (Leviticus 14:9), "and he shall wash his flesh in water, and be pure," and likewise (Leviticus 13:6), "and he shall wash his garments and be pure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:71: Purity is also found in garments, as our father Jacob, peace be upon him, said when he wished to come to Beit El (Genesis 35:2), "purify yourselves and change your garments." And although these seem to be two separate things — first, "purify yourselves" through immersion, and further, "and change your garments" — nevertheless, since he juxtaposed them, changing clothes is a category of purification, and it is fitting for one who wishes to purify himself that his garments be pure from soiling and impurity, and not be stained with oil or grease and the like — for they explained (Shabbat 114a) that a Torah scholar who is found with a grease stain on his garments is liable to death, as it is said (Proverbs 8:36), "all who hate me love death" — do not read "mesan'ai" [those who hate me] but "mesani'ai" [those who make me hated, i.e., through their appearance].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:72: So too the Rokeach, peace be upon him, wrote regarding the root of purity: be careful with the purity of your garments, that they not be soiled from excrement or drops of urine; guard your feet as you go to the House of God; therefore train yourself to wipe well, guard your orifices, and do not habitually urinate close to redemption [the Ge'ulah blessing before the Amidah], lest it drip onto your trousers — how would you pray "forgive us, for we have sinned," while you stand soiled? And be careful with seminal emission, lest it cling to your flesh and your garments; and your garments should not be from ornaments of idolatry; purify yourself, prepare to meet your God, O Israel. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:73: Further, purity is found regarding place, as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said to Aaron (Leviticus 10:14), "and the thigh of the offering you shall eat in a pure place"; and the Rashbi, peace be upon him, in parashat Terumah (128a), in the passage we quoted in chapter 5, said: and the spirit of holiness is not so, but rather [comes] in complete reward, in the rectification of one's own self, and in the purification of one's dwelling. Here, "the purification of his dwelling" is the purity of place, and "the rectification of his own self" is the meaning of "prepare to meet your God, O Israel." And without doubt, this preparation is also through immersion, as the Rokeach wrote.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:74: Further, regarding the purification of the metzora [leper], we find included in his purification the shaving of hair, as it is written (Leviticus 14:8), "and the one being purified shall wash his garments and shave off all his hair" — and the reason is that the hair of a young man's head represents the forces of judgment, and it is good to shave them, in the manner of (see Zohar, parashat Vayechi 217a), "before he shaves this, the head of his Master" [an obscure allusion] — and this is the secret of (Leviticus 13:40), "and if a man's head becomes bald, he is bald, he is pure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:75: Likewise it is good for purity to trim the fingernails, for a woman purifying herself for her husband must cut them, as explained in the Zohar, parashat Acharei Mot (79a) and parashat Pinchas (248b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:76: Further, one must purify himself from all the things mentioned as causing impurity in the Torah and in the words of our sages, of blessed memory, and I have already quoted most of them in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5, and there are further particulars that will be explained below, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:77: The essence of purity is what was explained above, that one purify himself from every sin and guilt, as it is written (Ezekiel 36:25), "and I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be pure from all your impurities, and from all your idols I will purify you" — surely this refers to the purification of the evil inclination, from whose side is the essence of impurity, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 51:4), "and purify me from my sin," and there are many similar verses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:78: So too our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 17a): it was a common saying in the mouth of Rabbi Meir: learn with all your heart and with all your soul to know My ways, and to be diligent at the doors of My Torah, and guard My Torah in your heart, and let My fear be before your eyes; guard your mouth from all sin, and purify yourself from all guilt and iniquity, and I will be with you in every place. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:79: A person must intend to purify his sins through drawing down supernal light from the place of whiteness, in his intention of the thirteen attributes of mercy, particularly in two of them, in which the purification of sins and their whitening is mentioned. In the second attribute, "who forgives iniquity [nosei avon]," it says in the Idra of Naso (132b): and one was dark, and it is washed in that light as one who washes in that deep river. And in the third attribute, "who passes over transgression [oveir al pesha]," they say there (133a) that of it is said (Job 37:21), "and a wind passed and purified them." And although all thirteen attributes have the property of sweetening judgments, in these two in particular the matter of purification is mentioned, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:80: Especially on Yom Kippur, which is a day of atonement to purify sins, as it is written (Leviticus 16:30), "for on this day He shall atone for you, to purify you from all your sins" — one must intend what has been said, that Yom Kippur is above, and Arich Anpin is revealed to purify and whiten our sins — this is "before the Lord you shall be purified."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:81: Further, purity is found regarding hands, as it says (Job 17:9), "and he that has clean hands shall grow stronger." And what we explained above regarding "clean of hands" is "turning from evil"; however, this "purity" mentioned refers to the fulfillment of "and do good" — namely, that he engage his hands in the commandments of tzitzit, tefillin, sukkah, lulav, and the like. And as for why the term "purity" is used here, since "purity" also appears to relate to "turning from evil" — the meaning of "purity" here is not that, but rather the term for the brightness of light, in the manner of (Exodus 24:10), "and like the very heaven for clarity [la-tohar]" — and "tohar" is the Hall of Nogah — and likewise the language of our sages, of blessed memory (Chullin 60b), "what use is a lamp at noon [be-tihara]?" And it is impossible for a person to attain brightness of light through turning from evil alone, but rather through his engaging in the commandments, supernal light in the World to Come is added to his hand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:82: Further, we find the Holy One, blessed be He, called "of purer eyes than to behold evil" (Habakkuk 1:13); and according to the way we explained regarding "clean of hands," we must say that not only does He not see evil, but He is pure in that His providence is always in holiness, for He is holy and His ministers are holy; and the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "of pure eyes," that His providence always stands in its brightness and does not spread out to the outside forces. And it is impossible to say of the Holy One, blessed be He, Heaven forbid, "clean eyes," which would suggest He had seen evil and needed cleansing — rather, He always stands in His purity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:83: However, according to what is explained in the Idra of Naso regarding the eye of Arich [Anpin], where it says (130a), we have learned, there is no illumination for the lower eye to be washed from redness, from blackness, except when it sees that this white light of the supernal eye, called "good eye" [shines upon it] — end of quotation — it follows that purity here means literally that the eyes are purified from the redness of judgment through the illumination of supernal light from the eye of Arich.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:84: We may say that both are true — for in being purified from judgment through the supernal light, brightness of light is added to them, and the word "purity" is used in Scripture in these two senses: either purifying a blemished thing so that it remains in its former whiteness as it was, or in adding illumination, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:85: A person must resemble his Maker in purifying his eyes from seeing evil, as will be explained in the rectification of the eyes — particularly, not gazing upon the image of a wicked man, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Megillah 28a): Rabbi Ami asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Karchah, by what merit have you lengthened your days? He said to him: in all my days I have never gazed upon the image of a wicked man. And anything that brings about length of days depends upon Arich Anpin; we find ourselves taught that the supernal eye does not watch over the wicked, as explained above — this being "of purer eyes than to behold evil."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:86: However, he should resemble his Maker in gazing upon everything that pertains to holiness — for just as His providence, blessed be He, is to bestow upon the holy, as it is written (Psalms 33:18), "behold, the eye of the Lord is upon those who fear Him" — and through this he causes the eye of Arich Anpin to illuminate the eyes of Ze'ir [Anpin]. It appears fitting to intend this when gazing upon a holy matter, and he will merit in the future that "eye to eye they shall see, when the Lord returns to Zion" (Isaiah 52:8); and so they say there (Zohar, parashat Naso 130a), and the righteous, meritorious ones above are destined to see with wisdom — this being what is written, "for eye to eye they shall see" — when? "When the Lord returns to Zion" — and it is written (Numbers 14:14), "that eye to eye You are seen, O Lord." — end of quotation. And without doubt only the righteous who guarded their eyes properly will merit this rank, as it says, "the righteous, meritorious ones above."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:87: Further, we find in "purity" a great matter pertaining to action — what our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yoma 72b) on the verse (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the Lord is pure" — in these words: Rabbi Yochanan said, this refers to one who studies Torah in purity — what is this? He marries a wife and then studies Torah. — end of quotation. Without doubt, in order for a person to attain clinging of his thought to his God, he must first marry a wife, and through this his thoughts will be purified; and without a wife it is impossible for him to attain any completeness, for he is lacking and blemished, possessing a defect — surely when he is married he is a complete person, as it is said (Genesis 5:2), "male and female He created them, and He called their name Adam [Man]" — as elaborated at length in parashat Vayikra (7b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:88: Further, we find purity regarding a table: "upon the pure table" (II Chronicles 13:11). Although this pertains to the matter of judgment, in that it is called "pure," as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 26b), nevertheless the Torah is expounded in many ways, and we may say that it is written "pure" to teach a moral lesson to man, that his table be pure — meaning, that he not be drawn after bodily pleasures stemming from the evil inclination, for a person's table is called an altar of atonement for him, and when he is not drawn after the pleasures of his inclination, surely by this he subdues his inclination, and it becomes an altar of atonement to purify his sins.
